comp-cvs-back-001.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-001.prompt: A lumbar pedicle screw breaches the medial cortex of the pedicle but remains within its vertical level. Which relationship best explains the immediate neural risk?
comp-cvs-back-001.learningObjective: Infer the direction of neural risk from the pedicle's relationship to the vertebral canal.

comp-cvs-back-002.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-002.prompt: Use the source figure to reason about the two altered boundaries. Imaging shows a posterolateral disc bulge projecting into an intervertebral foramen and an osteophyte projecting from the facet joint into that same foramen. Which opposing boundaries are jointly narrowing the nerve's exit passage?
comp-cvs-back-002.learningObjective: Integrate disc and facet pathology with the boundaries of the intervertebral foramen.

comp-cvs-back-003.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-003.prompt: A limited lumbar laminectomy enlarges space behind the thecal sac while preserving the vertebral body. Which combination correctly describes the removed structure and the principal load-bearing structure left intact?
comp-cvs-back-003.learningObjective: Relate decompressive laminectomy to canal architecture and axial load transmission.

comp-cvs-back-004.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-004.prompt: A vertebral-body metastasis causes collapse and a fragment moves posteriorly. A clinician is concerned about new bilateral leg deficits. Which anatomical sequence best explains this concern?
comp-cvs-back-004.learningObjective: Explain how vertebral-body collapse can produce a neurological lesion.

comp-cvs-back-005.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-005.prompt: After upper cervical trauma, the atlas and skull translate anteriorly relative to the axis while the dens remains attached to the axis. Failure of which restraint most directly permits loss of the normal atlas-dens relationship?
comp-cvs-back-005.learningObjective: Predict instability from disruption of the transverse ligament of the atlas.

comp-cvs-back-006.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-006.prompt: A ligamentous injury permits excessive rotation of the skull and atlas relative to the axis. The dens remains appropriately held against the anterior arch of the atlas. Which structures are most directly implicated?
comp-cvs-back-006.learningObjective: Distinguish the rotational restraint of the alar ligaments from the transverse ligament's role.

comp-cvs-back-007.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-007.prompt: An isolated injury greatly restricts turning the face left and right, but nodding remains relatively preserved. Which joint pairing best matches the lost movement and the preserved movement?
comp-cvs-back-007.learningObjective: Localize a selective head-movement deficit to the appropriate craniovertebral joint.

comp-cvs-back-008.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-008.prompt: A sagittal scan follows the posterior longitudinal ligament upward behind the axis. The same sheet continues from C2 toward the internal surface of the skull base. What is this superior continuation called?
comp-cvs-back-008.learningObjective: Trace the posterior longitudinal ligament into its craniovertebral continuation.

comp-cvs-back-009.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-009.prompt: A student compares thoracic and lumbar motion. Thoracic vertebrae permit useful rotation, whereas lumbar facets interlock and favor flexion-extension over large axial rotation. Which explanation best accounts for the regional difference?
comp-cvs-back-009.learningObjective: Explain regional spinal movement from facet geometry rather than joint-type misclassification.

comp-cvs-back-010.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-010.prompt: A fracture is confined to the transverse foramen of C7. Angiography shows an intact vertebral artery throughout its usual cervical course. Which anatomical fact makes these findings compatible?
comp-cvs-back-010.learningObjective: Use the usual C6 entry level to interpret a C7 transverse-foramen injury without ignoring vascular variants.

comp-cvs-back-011.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-011.prompt: During a lumbosacral dissection, a strong ligament joins the unusually large L5 transverse process to the iliac bone. Which stabilizing connection is being preserved?
comp-cvs-back-011.learningObjective: Relate the distinctive L5 transverse process to lumbopelvic stabilization.

comp-cvs-back-012.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-012.prompt: A sacral mass extends through the anterior S2 foramen while sparing the posterior S2 foramen. Which branch is directly endangered, and which broad distribution follows from that location?
comp-cvs-back-012.learningObjective: Infer the affected sacral ramus from anterior versus posterior foraminal involvement.

comp-cvs-back-013.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-013.prompt: An experimental disc retains a hydrated central nucleus but loses the normal lamellar organization of its outer ring. Which paired function is most directly impaired and relatively retained?
comp-cvs-back-013.learningObjective: Distinguish the mechanical contributions of annulus fibrosus and nucleus pulposus.

comp-cvs-back-014.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-014.prompt: During spinal flexion, adjacent laminae separate. A patient has extensive degeneration of the elastic tissue normally spanning those laminae. Which normal contribution would be reduced?
comp-cvs-back-014.learningObjective: Connect ligamentum flavum elasticity with flexion and return toward extension.

comp-cvs-back-015.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-015.prompt: A surgeon retracts the dural sac posteriorly and exposes a longitudinal ligament covering the posterior surfaces of lumbar vertebral bodies. Which statement correctly places that ligament?
comp-cvs-back-015.learningObjective: Resolve the apparently conflicting posterior-to-body and anterior-to-canal positions of the posterior longitudinal ligament.

comp-cvs-back-016.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-016.prompt: A midline fibrous sheet from the external occipital region to C7 becomes taut as the patient lowers the chin. Which feature explains its contribution to supporting the head?
comp-cvs-back-016.learningObjective: Explain head support using the attachments and function of ligamentum nuchae.

comp-cvs-back-017.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-017.prompt: An L4-L5 disc herniation projects posterolaterally within the lumbar canal and contacts a root descending past that disc to its exit below L5. Which root is compressed?
comp-cvs-back-017.learningObjective: Distinguish the traversing L5 root from the exiting L4 root at an L4-L5 disc.

comp-cvs-back-018.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-018.prompt: At the L4-L5 level, one patient has a disc fragment in the lateral recess contacting a descending L5 root. Another has a fragment within the L4-L5 intervertebral foramen contacting the exiting nerve. Which nerve is affected in the second patient?
comp-cvs-back-018.learningObjective: Use the position of a disc fragment, not only disc level, to identify a compressed lumbar nerve.

comp-cvs-back-019.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-019.prompt: A C5-C6 lesion narrows the intervertebral foramen. Which nerve is at risk, and why does the naming rule differ from that used below T1?
comp-cvs-back-019.learningObjective: Apply cervical nerve-exit nomenclature to foraminal narrowing.

comp-cvs-back-020.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-020.prompt: MRI shows a large central L4-L5 disc prolapse indenting the dural sac. The conus ends normally near L1-L2. Bilateral sacral sensory and sphincter symptoms develop. Which structure best accounts for these deficits at the imaged level?
comp-cvs-back-020.learningObjective: Explain multi-root sacral deficits from a central lower-lumbar canal lesion below the conus.

comp-cvs-back-021.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-021.prompt: A focal lesion interrupts a posterior root before it joins its anterior root. Testing shows a segmental sensory deficit without primary denervation of the corresponding skeletal muscles. Which comparison best explains this pattern?
comp-cvs-back-021.learningObjective: Distinguish a sensory root lesion from a mixed posterior-ramus lesion.

comp-cvs-back-022.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-022.prompt: After a local procedure, a narrow paraspinal skin strip loses sensation and the adjacent intrinsic back muscles become weak. Anterior trunk sensation and intercostal muscle function at that segment remain intact. Which lesion best fits?
comp-cvs-back-022.learningObjective: Localize a mixed paraspinal deficit to a posterior ramus while using spared functions as evidence.

comp-cvs-back-023.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-023.prompt: A lesion cuts an anterior root before it joins the posterior root. Which finding most strongly distinguishes this lesion from interruption of the whole spinal nerve just distal to their union?
comp-cvs-back-023.learningObjective: Compare anterior-root and mixed-spinal-nerve lesions using motor and sensory distributions.

comp-cvs-back-024.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-024.prompt: A patient has pain from a diseased posterior disc margin and adjacent dura. The responsible small nerves branch near the division of the spinal nerve and return through the intervertebral foramen. Which route is being described?
comp-cvs-back-024.learningObjective: Trace recurrent meningeal innervation to pain-sensitive vertebral-canal structures.

comp-cvs-back-025.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-025.prompt: A mass fills the foramen between C7 and T1. A report labels the affected nerve T1 solely because the lower vertebra is T1. Which correction follows normal spinal-nerve nomenclature?
comp-cvs-back-025.learningObjective: Apply the C8 transition to a cervicothoracic foraminal lesion.

comp-cvs-back-026.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-026.prompt: A thoracic spinal nerve is identified as T6 as it leaves below the T6 pedicle. Its small posterior ramus is intact, but its larger anterior ramus is divided. Which distribution should be most affected?
comp-cvs-back-026.learningObjective: Combine thoracic exit nomenclature with the functional distribution of the anterior ramus.

comp-cvs-back-027.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-027.prompt: A surgeon follows a normal S1 nerve root caudally from the lumbar cistern. Which observation is expected before it reaches its sacral exit?
comp-cvs-back-027.learningObjective: Explain the long intracanalar course of a sacral root using differential growth of cord and column.

comp-cvs-back-028.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-028.prompt: A painful vesicular eruption follows a single thoracic dermatome. Reactivation occurs in sensory neuron cell bodies, and symptoms extend into both anterior and posterior cutaneous territories of the segment. Which location can account for both territories?
comp-cvs-back-028.learningObjective: Relate a dermatomal sensory disorder to dorsal-root-ganglion anatomy across ramal territories.

comp-cvs-back-029.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-029.prompt: Two lesions are at the same L4 vertebral level in adults. One is within a normally positioned dural sac and the other within the vertebral body. Which neural tissue is normally available for direct compression inside the sac at that level?
comp-cvs-back-029.learningObjective: Distinguish vertebral level from spinal cord segment when interpreting a lumbar lesion.

comp-cvs-back-030.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-030.prompt: An MRI report describes a lumbosacral enlargement of the spinal cord superior to the conus. Why does the word 'lumbosacral' not establish that this enlargement lies opposite the lumbar and sacral vertebrae bearing the same numbers?
comp-cvs-back-030.learningObjective: Interpret cord enlargement names as segmental innervation relationships rather than matching vertebral levels.

comp-cvs-back-031.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-031.prompt: Imaging shows the cord tapering near L1-L2, but the CSF-containing meningeal sac continues to S2. Which combination best identifies these two endpoints?
comp-cvs-back-031.learningObjective: Separate cord termination from termination of the CSF-containing spinal meningeal sac.

comp-cvs-back-032.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-032.prompt: An adult lumbar puncture rationale is copied unchanged into a description of neonatal anatomy. Which correction is most relevant to the anatomical premise of avoiding cord injury?
comp-cvs-back-032.learningObjective: Recognize the age-dependent difference in conus position relevant to anatomical procedural reasoning.

comp-cvs-back-033.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-033.prompt: An epidural collection displaces an intact spinal dural sac inward. Which description correctly identifies the occupied compartment and explains why it can enlarge without first tearing dura?
comp-cvs-back-033.learningObjective: Locate spinal epidural pathology relative to the meninges and canal walls.

comp-cvs-back-034.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-034.prompt: During intradural exposure, a triangular process projects laterally from a longitudinal pial sheet between anterior and posterior rootlets and attaches through arachnoid to dura. What is its main anatomical role?
comp-cvs-back-034.learningObjective: Identify the origin, position and anchoring function of denticulate ligaments.

comp-cvs-back-035.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-035.prompt: A dissector follows the dural sleeve laterally along spinal roots through an intervertebral foramen. With which outer nerve covering does this sleeve become continuous?
comp-cvs-back-035.learningObjective: Trace the continuity from spinal dura to the peripheral nerve's outer covering.

comp-cvs-back-036.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-036.prompt: A midline filament descends from the conus within the lumbar cistern, acquires a dural investment near the end of the sac, and continues to the coccyx. Which interpretation best distinguishes it from adjacent cauda equina structures?
comp-cvs-back-036.learningObjective: Distinguish pial and dural parts of the filum terminale from cauda equina roots.

comp-cvs-back-037.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-037.prompt: For an anatomical model of a conventional midline lumbar puncture, which sequence correctly places the deeper tissues after the interspinous ligament and before free CSF is reached?
comp-cvs-back-037.learningObjective: Order the tissue planes traversed during a midline lumbar puncture.

comp-cvs-back-038.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-038.prompt: Use the source figure's meningeal relationships; the question concerns the lower lumbar cistern below the usual conus, not the pictured cord level. A lower lumbar needle passes beyond the epidural space and pierces two closely apposed membranes, after which clear CSF flows. Why is penetration of pia unnecessary for this result?
comp-cvs-back-038.learningObjective: Explain why CSF sampling does not require penetrating pia or spinal cord.

comp-cvs-back-039.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-039.prompt: In a surface-anatomy exercise, the intercristal line identifies approximately L4. Flexing the lumbar spine makes a route between adjacent posterior arches easier to visualize. Which explanation links these observations to lumbar access?
comp-cvs-back-039.learningObjective: Connect surface landmarks and flexion-dependent posterior spaces to the anatomical rationale for lower lumbar access.

comp-cvs-back-040.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-040.prompt: Use the source figure to infer which compartment has been reached. A needle stops just beyond the ligamentum flavum. Blood is aspirated, but no CSF is obtained. Imaging confirms that dura has not been crossed. Which structure most plausibly accounts for the blood?
comp-cvs-back-040.learningObjective: Use a needle's meningeal depth to identify an epidural vascular source.

comp-cvs-back-041.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-041.prompt: Use the source figure's relationship between longitudinal arteries and segmental feeders. During treatment of a descending aortic lesion, a major left lower-thoracic segmental feeder is interrupted. The longitudinal spinal arteries remain anatomically present, yet acute lower-cord ischemia follows. Which explanation is best?
comp-cvs-back-041.learningObjective: Explain lower-cord ischemia after loss of a major segmental medullary feeder despite patent longitudinal arteries.

comp-cvs-back-042.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-042.prompt: At one intervertebral foramen, an arterial branch follows a posterior root and ends in its supply. At another level, a larger branch reaches a longitudinal spinal artery on the cord. Which distinction is correct?
comp-cvs-back-042.learningObjective: Differentiate radicular supply from segmental medullary reinforcement by tracing the vessel's endpoint.

comp-cvs-back-043.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-043.prompt: After an anterior spinal arterial insult, a patient has major motor impairment while posterior-column modalities are relatively preserved. Which anatomical distribution best explains the dissociation?
comp-cvs-back-043.learningObjective: Relate dissociated cord deficits to anterior versus posterior spinal arterial territories.

comp-cvs-back-044.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-044.prompt: A malignancy spreads to vertebrae through communicating venous channels. Which feature of the vertebral venous system best supports a route that need not follow a single one-way peripheral-to-heart path?
comp-cvs-back-044.learningObjective: Explain a venous route of vertebral metastasis from communicating vertebral plexus anatomy.

comp-cvs-back-045.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-045.prompt: A posterior spinal exposure identifies three longitudinal erector-spinae columns. The lateral column follows rib angles, the middle column follows transverse processes, and the medial column links spinous processes. Which order is correct from lateral to medial?
comp-cvs-back-045.learningObjective: Use attachments to reconstruct the lateral-to-medial arrangement of erector spinae.

comp-cvs-back-046.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-046.prompt: With the pelvis fixed, unilateral right transversospinalis fibers pull upper spinous processes toward right transverse processes. How does this compare with unilateral right splenius action on the head?
comp-cvs-back-046.learningObjective: Contrast ipsilateral splenius rotation with contralateral trunk rotation by transversospinales.

comp-cvs-back-047.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-047.prompt: A deep lumbar muscle is especially well developed in this region and sends fibers from lateral bony origins to spinous processes two to four vertebrae above. Which muscle is most consistent with this description?
comp-cvs-back-047.learningObjective: Distinguish multifidus from neighboring intrinsic muscles using regional development and vertebral span.

comp-cvs-back-048.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-048.prompt: A short deep muscle connects adjacent lumbar spinous processes on either side of the interspinous ligament. It contributes to local extension and stabilization rather than spanning several vertebral levels. Which muscle is being described?
comp-cvs-back-048.learningObjective: Distinguish short intrinsic back muscles by their attachments and span.

comp-cvs-back-049.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-049.prompt: After a posterior-triangle neck injury, a patient has shoulder droop, a weak shrug and difficulty raising the arm fully overhead. Scapular protraction against resistance is preserved. Which localization best fits the combined findings?
comp-cvs-back-049.learningObjective: Localize a combined shrug and upward-rotation deficit while using preserved protraction to distinguish scapular muscle lesions.

comp-cvs-back-050.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-050.prompt: Following thoracodorsal-nerve injury, a climber cannot generate the usual force to pull the body upward with the hands fixed overhead. Which lost humeral actions most directly explain the deficit?
comp-cvs-back-050.learningObjective: Translate latissimus dorsi actions into a functional deficit when the upper limb is fixed.

comp-cvs-back-051.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-051.prompt: A patient can shrug strongly but has weak scapular retraction and a resting scapula displaced laterally. Which nerve-muscle relationship best accounts for this pattern?
comp-cvs-back-051.learningObjective: Differentiate rhomboid and trapezius weakness through preserved shrug and impaired retraction.

comp-cvs-back-052.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-052.prompt: Two posterior rib-attaching muscle sheets lie deep to rhomboids and latissimus dorsi. They receive anterior-ramus branches despite their position on the back. Which conclusion is anatomically sound?
comp-cvs-back-052.learningObjective: Distinguish extrinsic intermediate back muscles from intrinsic muscles despite overlapping posterior location.

comp-cvs-back-053.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-053.prompt: A surgeon exposes a triangle bounded by rectus capitis posterior major, obliquus capitis superior and obliquus capitis inferior. Which combination should be anticipated within it?
comp-cvs-back-053.learningObjective: Use suboccipital triangle boundaries to anticipate its neurovascular contents.

comp-cvs-back-054.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-054.prompt: A short suboccipital muscle runs from the spinous process of C2 to the transverse process of C1 and has no direct attachment to the skull. How can it still rotate the face?
comp-cvs-back-054.learningObjective: Explain head rotation by obliquus capitis inferior from its atlas-axis attachments.

comp-cvs-back-055.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-055.prompt: A lesion injures the C1 posterior ramus within the suboccipital triangle, while the greater occipital nerve is preserved. Which combination is most likely?
comp-cvs-back-055.learningObjective: Separate C1 suboccipital motor supply from C2 greater-occipital cutaneous supply.

comp-cvs-back-056.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-056.prompt: After ascending through cervical transverse foramina, an artery turns through the deep suboccipital region before entering the skull. An injury between the artery and the posterior arch of C1 also threatens a nearby nerve. Which pairing is correct?
comp-cvs-back-056.learningObjective: Integrate the vertebral arterial route with the nearby C1 posterior-ramus relationship.

comp-cvs-back-057.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-057.prompt: A young athlete has bilateral defects in the region between the superior and inferior articular processes of L5, followed by anterior displacement of L5 relative to the sacrum. Which sequence best describes the anatomical failure?
comp-cvs-back-057.learningObjective: Relate a pars interarticularis defect to the potential for anterior vertebral slip without treating it as the only cause.

comp-cvs-back-058.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-058.prompt: Lumbar imaging shows a modest posterior disc protrusion from the anterior canal wall, together with posterior ligamentum-flavum thickening and enlarged facet joints. Why can the combined lesion cause more neural compromise than the disc finding alone suggests?
comp-cvs-back-058.learningObjective: Integrate disc, facet and ligamentum-flavum contributions to lumbar canal stenosis.

comp-cvs-back-059.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-059.prompt: Patient A has an intradural lesion at the tapering end of the cord, symmetric saddle sensory loss and early sphincter dysfunction. Patient B has a large lower-lumbar disc lesion, asymmetric leg and saddle deficits and later sphincter dysfunction. Which localization best fits the combined anatomical and clinical information?
comp-cvs-back-059.learningObjective: Differentiate terminal-cord and cauda-equina lesions by combining imaging location, symmetry and pelvic-function timing.

comp-cvs-back-060.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-060.prompt: An infection erodes a lumbar vertebral body and adjacent disc, extends anteriorly into a muscle sheath, and later produces a groin swelling beneath the inguinal ligament. Which anatomical route best unifies the spinal and groin findings?
comp-cvs-back-060.learningObjective: Use psoas fascial continuity to link a lumbar vertebral infection with a groin collection.

comp-cvs-back-061.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-061.prompt: On a lumbar transverse section, a muscle mass lies between the posterior and middle thoracolumbar fascial layers. A separate muscle lies between the middle and anterior layers. Which pairing correctly identifies them?
comp-cvs-back-061.learningObjective: Reconstruct lumbar muscle compartments from the three thoracolumbar fascial layers.

comp-cvs-back-062.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-062.prompt: A dissector follows the posterior and middle thoracolumbar fascial layers laterally until they unite, then follows the anterior layer joining near the lateral border of quadratus lumborum. Which muscle gains an aponeurotic origin from this merged structure?
comp-cvs-back-062.learningObjective: Trace thoracolumbar fascial continuity into the abdominal wall.

comp-cvs-back-063.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-063.prompt: A sagittal spine model preserves the embryonic curvature in two adult regions while adding curvatures that help align body weight for upright posture. Which set correctly distinguishes them?
comp-cvs-back-063.learningObjective: Connect primary and secondary sagittal curvatures to developmental origin and upright balance.

comp-cvs-back-064.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-back-064.prompt: A patient has an abnormal lateral spinal curve accompanied by rotation of the vertebrae, rather than simply an exaggerated posterior thoracic convexity on the sagittal view. Which interpretation best fits?
comp-cvs-back-064.learningObjective: Distinguish scoliosis with rotation from sagittal kyphotic or lordotic curvature changes.

comp-cvs-thorax-001.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-001.prompt: Rupture of one mitral papillary muscle compromises chordal support to regions of both mitral leaflets. Which anatomical arrangement explains why injury is not confined to just one leaflet?
comp-cvs-thorax-001.learningObjective: Explain mitral leaflet support by tracing chordae from each papillary muscle to both leaflets.

comp-cvs-thorax-002.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-002.prompt: A ventricular specimen has a valve leaflet tethered directly to the interventricular septum by individual true chordae. Which interpretation is best supported?
comp-cvs-thorax-002.learningObjective: Use direct septal chordal attachments to distinguish right from left ventricular valve support.

comp-cvs-thorax-003.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-003.prompt: During aortic-root reconstruction, the surgeon preserves a fibrous curtain shared with another valve. Which pairing correctly identifies that continuity and the valve relatively separated by its muscular outflow support?
comp-cvs-thorax-003.learningObjective: Relate aortic-root surgery to aortic-mitral fibrous continuity and pulmonary infundibular separation.

comp-cvs-thorax-004.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-004.prompt: A small surgical lesion at the junction of the membranous and muscular interventricular septum produces atrioventricular conduction failure even though the sinuatrial node remains active. Which local relationship best explains this?
comp-cvs-thorax-004.learningObjective: Predict conduction injury from the relationship of the atrioventricular bundle to the membranous-muscular septal junction.

comp-cvs-thorax-005.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-005.prompt: A markedly enlarged left atrium indents the esophagus. Which spatial relationship also makes transesophageal imaging useful for examining this chamber?
comp-cvs-thorax-005.learningObjective: Connect the left atrium's posterior relation to the esophagus with compression and imaging access.

comp-cvs-thorax-006.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-006.prompt: A proximal anterior interventricular artery occlusion occurs before its first septal perforator. New intraventricular conduction disturbance accompanies anterior septal injury. Which branch territory best links these findings?
comp-cvs-thorax-006.learningObjective: Integrate anterior septal arterial supply with the arterial vulnerability of the branching conduction bundle.

comp-cvs-thorax-007.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-007.prompt: Angiography shows a circumflex artery continuing through the cardiac crux as the posterior interventricular artery. An occlusion near that crux is followed by atrioventricular nodal dysfunction. Which inference is best?
comp-cvs-thorax-007.learningObjective: Use demonstrated coronary dominance to infer the likely AV nodal arterial vulnerability.

comp-cvs-thorax-008.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-008.prompt: An artery leaves the circumflex in the atrioventricular groove and runs toward the apex over the rounded left cardiac border. Focal occlusion chiefly threatens adjacent lateral left ventricular myocardium. Which artery is implicated?
comp-cvs-thorax-008.learningObjective: Trace the left marginal artery from its parent groove to its ventricular territory.

comp-cvs-thorax-009.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-009.prompt: A conal artery arises separately from the right aortic sinus and anastomoses with a conal branch of the anterior interventricular artery around the right ventricular outflow. Which interpretation is most accurate?
comp-cvs-thorax-009.learningObjective: Distinguish a conal arterial variant and collateral pathway from coronary dominance and fistula anatomy.

comp-cvs-thorax-010.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-010.prompt: A coronary segment is seen to run beneath a band of myocardium instead of remaining entirely in subepicardial fat. Which observation most directly supports myocardial bridging rather than a change in coronary origin?
comp-cvs-thorax-010.learningObjective: Separate coronary course variants from origin, dominance and venous-drainage variants.

comp-cvs-thorax-011.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-011.prompt: Dissection of the joint at the head of a typical rib reveals two synovial compartments. Which attachment separates them and fits the rib's articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies?
comp-cvs-thorax-011.learningObjective: Explain the two compartments of a typical rib-head joint from its intra-articular ligament.

comp-cvs-thorax-012.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-012.prompt: At a lower rib, imaging shows a head articulation with the vertebral column but no joint between a tubercle and a transverse process. Which interpretation most directly fits a normal floating rib?
comp-cvs-thorax-012.learningObjective: Differentiate normal floating-rib joint anatomy from a presumed pathological absence of a costotransverse joint.

comp-cvs-thorax-013.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-013.prompt: Near the sternum, a surgeon encounters an external intercostal membrane overlying muscular internal intercostal tissue. Near the rib angle posteriorly, the internal layer becomes membranous. Which explanation is correct?
comp-cvs-thorax-013.learningObjective: Reconstruct the layered thoracic wall from the unequal extents of the intercostal muscles and membranes.

comp-cvs-thorax-014.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-014.prompt: On the internal posterior thoracic wall, a muscle slip near a rib angle crosses to the second or third rib below. The intercostal vessels and nerve lie superficial to it, and pleura lies deeper. Which structure best fits?
comp-cvs-thorax-014.learningObjective: Identify a thoracic muscle from its span, wall position and neurovascular plane.

comp-cvs-thorax-015.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-015.prompt: A proximal subclavian lesion affects branches to the first two posterior intercostal spaces and the anterior intercostal supply, while the third through eleventh posterior intercostal origins remain patent. Which source pattern explains this?
comp-cvs-thorax-015.learningObjective: Integrate upper posterior and anterior thoracic-wall arterial origins with a proximal subclavian lesion.

comp-cvs-thorax-016.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-016.prompt: After axillary node surgery, a patient has numbness over the upper medial arm but normal intrinsic hand strength and normal finger sensation. Which injury best fits the distribution and spared function?
comp-cvs-thorax-016.learningObjective: Differentiate intercostobrachial sensory injury from lower-plexus and scapular motor-nerve lesions.

comp-cvs-thorax-017.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-017.prompt: A lesion of a lower intercostal nerve produces both thoracic-wall sensory change and weakness in part of the abdominal wall. Which explanation is anatomically appropriate?
comp-cvs-thorax-017.learningObjective: Explain combined thoracic and abdominal deficits from a lower intercostal-nerve lesion.

comp-cvs-thorax-018.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-018.prompt: A diagram shows one communicating branch carrying myelinated sympathetic fibers from a thoracic spinal nerve toward the sympathetic trunk, and another returning unmyelinated fibers toward the spinal nerve. Which pairing is correct?
comp-cvs-thorax-018.learningObjective: Distinguish white and gray rami communicantes by fiber class and route.

comp-cvs-thorax-019.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-019.prompt: A nerve leaves several lower thoracic sympathetic ganglia, descends on vertebral bodies and pierces a diaphragmatic crus toward the celiac region. Which description best distinguishes it from a cardiac sympathetic nerve?
comp-cvs-thorax-019.learningObjective: Compare thoracic splanchnic and cardiac sympathetic routes using synapse level and diaphragmatic passage.

comp-cvs-thorax-020.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-020.prompt: Two efferent fibers are traced toward the heart: one from a cervical sympathetic ganglion and one in a vagal cardiac branch. Which comparison correctly locates their next synaptic requirement?
comp-cvs-thorax-020.learningObjective: Distinguish sympathetic and vagal cardiac efferents by ganglionic relay location.

comp-cvs-thorax-021.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-021.prompt: During esophageal surgery, a thin channel is followed from a position between the azygos vein and descending aorta, across behind the esophagus around the mid-thoracic region, then toward the left venous angle. Which combined relationship supports its identification?
comp-cvs-thorax-021.learningObjective: Identify the thoracic duct through a sequence of spatial relationships rather than a single label.

comp-cvs-thorax-022.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-022.prompt: A nerve is preserved behind the left lung root, followed onto the anterior esophageal plexus, and then traced through the esophageal hiatus. Which final description is most accurate?
comp-cvs-thorax-022.learningObjective: Trace the left vagus through the esophageal plexus without incorrectly treating vagal trunks as unmixed unilateral nerves.

comp-cvs-thorax-023.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-023.prompt: Portal hypertension enlarges distal esophageal venous channels that connect with systemic thoracic veins. Which route best links the portal side to the superior caval side?
comp-cvs-thorax-023.learningObjective: Trace the distal esophageal portosystemic venous anastomosis responsible for variceal pathways.

comp-cvs-thorax-024.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-024.prompt: A deep neck infection tracks inferiorly along fascial planes and reaches the mediastinum despite no direct thoracic-wall wound. Which anatomical feature best explains the spread?
comp-cvs-thorax-024.learningObjective: Explain descending mediastinal spread through continuous cervical and thoracic fascial spaces.

comp-cvs-thorax-025.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-025.prompt: A dissection plane is posterior to the aortic arch, anterior to the tracheal bifurcation and superior to the pulmonary-trunk division. Which autonomic network occupies this relationship?
comp-cvs-thorax-025.learningObjective: Differentiate deep and superficial cardiac plexus positions from neighboring autonomic pathways.

comp-cvs-thorax-026.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-026.prompt: Inspiration dilates the opening around the inferior vena cava, while the aorta is normally not compressed by diaphragmatic muscle contraction. Which pairing best explains the different behavior?
comp-cvs-thorax-026.learningObjective: Explain different respiratory effects on caval and aortic passage from the tissue composition of their openings.

comp-cvs-thorax-027.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-027.prompt: A patient loses part of the external diaphragmatic contribution to the antireflux barrier after division of muscle around the esophageal hiatus. Which structure is principally involved?
comp-cvs-thorax-027.learningObjective: Identify the crural contribution to the esophageal antireflux barrier while distinguishing it from other diaphragmatic openings.

comp-cvs-thorax-028.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-028.prompt: A posterior diaphragmatic dissection follows an arch over psoas major and another more lateral arch over quadratus lumborum. The sympathetic trunk passes into the abdomen deep to the medial arch. Which naming sequence is correct?
comp-cvs-thorax-028.learningObjective: Distinguish median, medial and lateral arcuate structures using their underlying muscles and vessels.

comp-cvs-thorax-029.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-029.prompt: Inflammation confined to the central diaphragmatic peritoneal region produces shoulder referral, whereas irritation confined to the peripheral diaphragm is felt near the lower thoracic wall. Which innervation contrast best explains the difference?
comp-cvs-thorax-029.learningObjective: Use central versus peripheral diaphragmatic sensory supply to explain different pain distributions.

comp-cvs-thorax-030.subject: anatomy
comp-cvs-thorax-030.prompt: In patient A, the gastroesophageal junction migrates above the diaphragm. In patient B, a portion of stomach herniates beside the esophagus while that junction remains normally positioned. Which anatomical classification fits?
comp-cvs-thorax-030.learningObjective: Distinguish sliding from paraesophageal hiatus hernia by the position of the gastroesophageal junction.

comp-cvs-phys-001.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-001.prompt: Vagal stimulation makes the maximum diastolic potential more negative while the threshold remains similar. Which combination explains a slower sinus rate and impaired AV conduction?
comp-cvs-phys-001.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Increased potassium permeability delays threshold attainment and reduces nodal excitability.

comp-cvs-phys-002.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-002.prompt: Complete AV block begins abruptly. The atria continue at 80/min, but ventricular activity resumes only after several seconds at 30/min. What explains both the pause and the new rate?
comp-cvs-phys-002.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Previously overdriven subsidiary pacemakers recover and discharge at a slower intrinsic rate.

comp-cvs-phys-003.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-003.prompt: A preparation retains normal atrial activation and AV delay, but ventricular excitation spreads slowly from cell to cell after loss of effective Purkinje conduction. What paired change is expected?
comp-cvs-phys-003.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: A broader QRS and less synchronous ventricular contraction.

comp-cvs-phys-004.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-004.prompt: In a ring of excitable cardiac tissue with unidirectional block, circuit length is 12 cm, conduction velocity 40 cm/s, and refractory period 0.20 s. Will a wave returning to its starting point find recovered tissue?
comp-cvs-phys-004.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Yes: circuit transit is 0.30 s, exceeding the 0.20-s refractory period.

comp-cvs-phys-005.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-005.prompt: A viable 12-cm reentry circuit initially conducts at 40 cm/s with a 0.20-s refractory period. An intervention prolongs refractoriness to 0.36 s but also slows conduction to 25 cm/s. With the path and unidirectional block unchanged, which prediction follows from the new timing?
comp-cvs-phys-005.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Reentry can persist: the new 0.48-s transit still exceeds the 0.36-s refractory period.

comp-cvs-phys-006.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-006.prompt: An ECG shows progressively longer PR intervals followed by a nonconducted P wave, then a shorter PR interval. Which explanation best links the sequence to its usual site?
comp-cvs-phys-006.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Progressively delayed AV nodal conduction culminating in a Wenckebach dropped beat.

comp-cvs-phys-008.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-008.prompt: During ventricular fibrillation the tracing contains abundant electrical activity, yet arterial pulsations disappear. Why does electrical activity not imply effective cardiac output?
comp-cvs-phys-008.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Spatially disorganized excitation fails to produce coordinated filling and ejection.

comp-cvs-phys-009.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-009.prompt: The mean QRS is equiphasic in aVR (axis −150°) and predominantly positive in lead I. Which of the two perpendicular directions is consistent?
comp-cvs-phys-009.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Approximately −60°.

comp-cvs-phys-010.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-010.prompt: Lead I has a net-positive QRS, aVF net-negative, and lead II net-negative. Using the lead axes and ignoring equiphasic boundary cases, which narrower interval contains the mean QRS axis?
comp-cvs-phys-010.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Between −90° and −30°.

comp-cvs-phys-011.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-011.prompt: An instantaneous ventricular vector has magnitude 2 mV and points +60°. What simultaneous voltage is projected onto lead I, ignoring other sources?
comp-cvs-phys-011.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: +1 mV.

comp-cvs-phys-012.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-012.prompt: At a paper speed of 50 mm/s, the PR interval occupies eight small horizontal 1-mm squares. What is its duration, and what error results from assuming 25 mm/s?
comp-cvs-phys-012.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: 0.16 s; assuming 25 mm/s falsely doubles it to 0.32 s.

comp-cvs-phys-013.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-013.prompt: A 1-mV calibration pulse is 5 mm tall and an R wave is 8 mm tall. What amplitude should be reported before applying voltage criteria?
comp-cvs-phys-013.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: 1.6 mV.

comp-cvs-phys-014.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-014.prompt: A patient with increased ventricular wall thickness has unexpectedly low limb-lead QRS voltage. Which inference is justified from these findings alone?
comp-cvs-phys-014.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Surface voltage is influenced by tissue properties and the surrounding conductor, so low voltage does not exclude increased wall thickness.

comp-cvs-phys-015.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-015.prompt: Two patients have low-voltage ECGs: one has a large pericardial effusion, the other marked pulmonary hyperinflation. Which comparison matches the book’s physical explanation?
comp-cvs-phys-015.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Fluid redistributes conducted current around the heart; excess lung air impedes its transmission to the surface.

comp-cvs-phys-016.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-016.prompt: Atrial depolarization is visible as a P wave, but a separate atrial repolarization wave is usually absent. Which timing relationship best explains this?
comp-cvs-phys-016.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Atrial repolarization usually overlaps the much larger ventricular QRS complex.

comp-cvs-phys-017.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-017.prompt: After selective arterial baroreceptor denervation, a subject has much larger pressure swings during posture and excitement. Which conclusion is strongest?
comp-cvs-phys-017.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Loss of rapid negative feedback increases pressure variability; it does not by itself specify a permanently fixed hypertensive pressure.

comp-cvs-phys-018.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-018.prompt: An isolated carotid sinus is held at low pressure while other inputs are controlled, producing a systemic pressor response. The central afferent pathway is then electrically stimulated to a high firing rate without changing the low sinus pressure. What happens to the original reflex tendency?
comp-cvs-phys-018.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: It is opposed: increased afferent signaling suppresses sympathetic output despite the unchanged low pressure at the receptor.

comp-cvs-phys-019.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-019.prompt: During sustained hypertension, mechanically evoked carotid baroreceptor firing partly returns toward baseline. Yet prolonged electrical stimulation of carotid afferents still produces sustained reductions in sympathetic activity and pressure. Which inference best reconciles the two observations?
comp-cvs-phys-019.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Much resetting occurs at the pressure-sensitive endings; a responsive afferent–central pathway can still influence renal sympathetic activity and sustained pressure.

comp-cvs-phys-020.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-020.prompt: A volume infusion increases atrial stretch but also raises arterial pressure. Why is the direction of the heart-rate change not fixed by atrial stretch alone?
comp-cvs-phys-020.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: The tachycardic Bainbridge tendency competes with arterial baroreflex slowing.

comp-cvs-phys-021.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-021.prompt: Following volume expansion, renal sympathetic activity and ADH fall while atrial natriuretic peptide rises. What integrated result opposes the initiating disturbance?
comp-cvs-phys-021.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Greater renal salt and water excretion reduces the excess circulating volume.

comp-cvs-phys-022.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-022.prompt: In a simplified pressure–natriuresis model, renal excretion is E = (P − 60)/40, where E is in units of baseline salt intake and P is arterial pressure in mmHg. The curve shifts rightward by 25 mmHg without changing slope, and intake rises from 1.0 to 1.25 units. Ignoring nonrenal losses, what is the new equilibrium pressure?
comp-cvs-phys-022.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: 135 mmHg.

comp-cvs-phys-023.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-023.prompt: In a volume-loading experiment, cardiac output rises early but later returns toward baseline while pressure remains elevated. Which accompanying change explains the later pressure?
comp-cvs-phys-023.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: A secondary rise in total peripheral resistance associated with tissue autoregulation.

comp-cvs-phys-024.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-024.prompt: Renal perfusion pressure and macula-densa NaCl delivery both fall while renal sympathetic activity rises. Which sequence most accurately predicts the downstream pressure-supporting response?
comp-cvs-phys-024.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Renin release increases, generating angiotensin II with rapid vasoconstrictor and slower salt-retaining effects.

comp-cvs-phys-025.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-025.prompt: In a simplified preparation, cardiac output = 2 + PRA and venous return = (10 − PRA)/2, with flows in L/min and PRA in mmHg. What is the steady operating point?
comp-cvs-phys-025.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: PRA = 2 mmHg and flow = 4 L/min.

comp-cvs-phys-026.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-026.prompt: With venous-return parameters unchanged, a pure increase in cardiac pumping effectiveness raises the cardiac function curve. Before reflex or volume changes, what is the usual new intersection?
comp-cvs-phys-026.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Higher flow at a lower right atrial pressure.

comp-cvs-phys-027.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-027.prompt: Resistance to venous return doubles while mean systemic filling pressure remains 8 mmHg. What happens to the descending venous-return curve?
comp-cvs-phys-027.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Its slope magnitude halves while its zero-flow PRA intercept remains 8 mmHg.

comp-cvs-phys-028.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-028.prompt: Right atrial pressure becomes progressively more negative, but venous return eventually plateaus despite a nominally larger upstream-to-atrium gradient. Why does the simple linear equation stop predicting increasing flow?
comp-cvs-phys-028.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Collapse of large veins near the thorax limits additional flow.

comp-cvs-phys-029.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-032.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-036.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-036.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Impaired filling can limit stroke volume despite a preserved ejected fraction.

comp-cvs-phys-037.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-039.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: 4.5 L/min.

comp-cvs-phys-040.subject: physiology
comp-cvs-phys-040.prompt: A dilated left ventricle develops mitral regurgitation despite initially intact valve leaflets. Which mechanism links ventricular geometry to a systolic apical murmur?

comp-cvs-phys-041.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-041.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Compensatory vasoconstriction can preserve pressure despite reduced flow.

comp-cvs-phys-042.subject: physiology

comp-cvs-phys-044.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism and distinguish adjacent alternatives: Increased vascular capacity plus loss of intravascular fluid from increased permeability.

cvs-3d-022.learningObjective: Identify the Brachiocephalic trunk in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

cvs-3d-023.learningObjective: Identify the Left common carotid artery in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

cvs-3d-024.subject: anatomy
cvs-3d-024.prompt: In the interactive 3D mediastinum & great vessels model, which structure is highlighted?
cvs-3d-024.learningObjective: Identify the Left subclavian artery in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.
