cvs-3d-025.learningObjective: Identify the Azygos vein in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

cvs-3d-026.subject: anatomy
cvs-3d-026.prompt: In the interactive 3D mediastinum & great vessels model, which structure is highlighted?
cvs-3d-026.learningObjective: Identify the Thoracic duct in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

cvs-3d-027.subject: anatomy
cvs-3d-027.prompt: In the interactive 3D mediastinum model, which structure is highlighted?
cvs-3d-027.learningObjective: Identify the Left recurrent laryngeal nerve in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

cvs-3d-028.subject: anatomy
cvs-3d-028.prompt: In the interactive 3D mediastinum model, which structure is highlighted?
cvs-3d-028.learningObjective: Identify the Left phrenic nerve in the interactive CVS model and distinguish it from nearby structures.

depth-cvs-anat-001.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-001.prompt: During ablation near the coronary sinus ostium, the catheter is kept away from the apex of the triangle bounded by the tendon of Todaro, septal tricuspid leaflet and coronary sinus opening. Which structure is chiefly at risk there?
depth-cvs-anat-001.learningObjective: Use the boundaries of the triangle of Koch to localize the atrioventricular node.

depth-cvs-anat-002.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-002.prompt: A surgeon follows the muscular ridge that separates the tricuspid inflow region from the smooth pulmonary outflow tract of the right ventricle. Which ridge is being followed?
depth-cvs-anat-002.learningObjective: Distinguish the right-ventricular inflow and outflow regions by their separating landmark.

depth-cvs-anat-003.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-003.prompt: From inside the right atrium, a probe presses on the thin floor of the fossa ovalis. Which embryological septum principally forms this floor in the adult?
depth-cvs-anat-003.learningObjective: Relate adult fossa-ovalis morphology to the overlapping fetal septa.

depth-cvs-anat-004.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-004.prompt: A fibrous barrier electrically separates atrial from ventricular myocardium. Which normal structure penetrates this barrier to provide the conducting connection between the two?
depth-cvs-anat-004.learningObjective: Explain how the fibrous skeleton isolates atrial and ventricular myocardium while permitting normal conduction.

depth-cvs-anat-005.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-005.prompt: A catheter passes from the left ventricular cavity toward the aortic valve through a smooth-walled outflow region. What is this region called?
depth-cvs-anat-005.learningObjective: Differentiate the smooth outflow tracts of the right and left ventricles.

depth-cvs-anat-006.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-006.prompt: Venous blood from the anterior wall of the right ventricle reaches the right atrium without entering the coronary sinus. Which vessels provide this route?
depth-cvs-anat-006.learningObjective: Distinguish direct right-atrial venous return from tributaries of the coronary sinus.

depth-cvs-anat-007.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-007.prompt: Contrast injection shows minute valveless channels opening directly from myocardium into several cardiac chambers. Which vessels are these?
depth-cvs-anat-007.learningObjective: Recognize the direct intramyocardial venous pathway formed by the smallest cardiac veins.

depth-cvs-anat-008.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-008.prompt: A vein ascends beside the anterior interventricular artery, then turns into the left atrioventricular groove before continuing toward the coronary sinus. Which vein follows this course?
depth-cvs-anat-008.learningObjective: Trace the great cardiac vein by its changing arterial relationships.

depth-cvs-anat-009.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-009.prompt: In the most common coronary pattern, an occlusion near the cardiac crux threatens the artery to the atrioventricular node. From which coronary artery does that nodal branch usually arise?
depth-cvs-anat-009.learningObjective: Relate coronary dominance at the crux to the usual arterial supply of the atrioventricular node.

depth-cvs-anat-010.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-010.prompt: A right-coronary angiogram does not show a sinuatrial nodal branch, yet the node enhances normally. Which alternative origin best accounts for this finding?
depth-cvs-anat-010.learningObjective: Recognize the important variable coronary origins of the sinuatrial nodal artery.

depth-cvs-anat-011.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-011.prompt: During a lateral pericardial dissection, a nerve and accompanying vessels are found in the plane between fibrous pericardium and mediastinal parietal pleura. Which bundle is this?
depth-cvs-anat-011.learningObjective: Identify the neurovascular plane that must be protected during lateral pericardial access.

depth-cvs-anat-012.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-012.prompt: For a subxiphoid pericardiocentesis, a needle is introduced between the xiphisternum and left costal margin at about 45 degrees. Toward which landmark is it directed?
depth-cvs-anat-012.learningObjective: Apply the surface trajectory for subxiphoid pericardial access.

depth-cvs-anat-013.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-013.prompt: A mediastinal surgeon identifies two major nerves at a lung root. Which relationship correctly distinguishes them?
depth-cvs-anat-013.learningObjective: Use anterior-posterior lung-root relationships to distinguish phrenic from vagus nerves.

depth-cvs-anat-014.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-014.prompt: A mass expands in the aortopulmonary interval between the aortic arch and left pulmonary artery. Which nerve is especially vulnerable as it hooks beneath the arch beside the ligamentum arteriosum?
depth-cvs-anat-014.learningObjective: Localize the left recurrent laryngeal nerve from its relation to the aortic arch and pulmonary artery.

depth-cvs-anat-015.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-015.prompt: On the left side of the aortic arch, a vein ascends to the left brachiocephalic vein between the vagus medially and phrenic nerve laterally. Which vein has this characteristic course?
depth-cvs-anat-015.learningObjective: Use nerve and aortic-arch relationships to identify the left superior intercostal vein.

depth-cvs-anat-016.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-016.prompt: A thoracic-duct injury below the level where the duct crosses from right to left is most likely to produce which initial pleural collection?
depth-cvs-anat-016.learningObjective: Infer the side of chylothorax from the thoracic duct's mediastinal crossing.

depth-cvs-anat-017.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-017.prompt: At T8-T9 a left-sided vein crosses the midline posterior to both the oesophagus and descending thoracic aorta before joining the azygos vein. Which vessel is it?
depth-cvs-anat-017.learningObjective: Identify a posterior-mediastinal vein from its vertebral level and relationships during its midline crossing.

depth-cvs-anat-018.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-018.prompt: Inferior vena caval obstruction below the liver enlarges a longitudinal collateral route that links ascending lumbar veins to the superior vena cava. Which thoracic system carries this bypass?
depth-cvs-anat-018.learningObjective: Explain why the azygos system enlarges when inferior caval flow is obstructed.

depth-cvs-anat-019.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-019.prompt: An artery descending with the phrenic nerve supplies the fibrous and parietal pericardium. From which parent vessel does it usually arise?
depth-cvs-anat-019.learningObjective: Link the pericardial arterial supply to the internal thoracic artery and phrenic nerve.

depth-cvs-anat-020.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-020.prompt: In chronic aortic coarctation distal to the left subclavian artery, which sequence provides a major collateral route from proximal to distal aorta?
depth-cvs-anat-020.learningObjective: Reconstruct the intercostal arterial collateral pathway around aortic coarctation.

depth-cvs-anat-021.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-021.prompt: A carcinoma in the medial breast spreads to nodes beside the internal thoracic vessels and then appears in the opposite breast. Which anatomical feature best permits this pattern?
depth-cvs-anat-021.learningObjective: Use parasternal lymphatic anatomy to explain contralateral spread from a medial breast lesion.

depth-cvs-anat-022.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-022.prompt: A breast mass is freely mobile over pectoralis major. Preservation of which plane most directly accounts for this mobility?
depth-cvs-anat-022.learningObjective: Relate clinical breast mobility to the retromammary plane.

depth-cvs-anat-023.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-023.prompt: A surgeon must avoid both the main and collateral intercostal bundles. Where are these bundles concentrated within a typical interspace?
depth-cvs-anat-023.learningObjective: Integrate main and collateral intercostal bundle positions for safe incisions.

depth-cvs-anat-024.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-024.prompt: In the conventional surface-anatomy teaching scheme, which set of landmarks is associated with the transverse thoracic plane through the sternal angle?
depth-cvs-anat-024.learningObjective: Integrate airway, arterial and mediastinal landmarks at the sternal-angle plane.

depth-cvs-anat-025.subject: anatomy
depth-cvs-anat-025.prompt: On axial imaging, an enlarged subaortic nodal station occupies the aortopulmonary interval. Which pair forms its principal superior and inferior boundaries?
depth-cvs-anat-025.learningObjective: Recognize the aortopulmonary interval on cross-sectional mediastinal anatomy.

depth-cvs-emb-001.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-001.prompt: Anterior endoderm continues to secrete BMP2 and BMP4, but an experimental embryo cannot produce CRESCENT or CERBERUS in endoderm adjacent to the cardiogenic mesoderm. Which immediate developmental result is most likely?
depth-cvs-emb-001.learningObjective: Integrate BMP and WNT signaling in induction of the cardiogenic mesoderm.

depth-cvs-emb-002.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-002.prompt: A teratogen causes uniformly high retinoic-acid signaling along the early heart-forming region instead of the normal caudal-to-cranial difference. Which regional identity would be most directly overfavored?
depth-cvs-emb-002.learningObjective: Predict cardiac regional identity from the retinoic-acid gradient.

depth-cvs-emb-003.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-003.prompt: NKX2.5 is expressed normally, but HAND1 expression is selectively lost while HAND2 remains confined to its usual ventricular territory. Which defect is most directly predicted?
depth-cvs-emb-003.learningObjective: Relate HAND1 and HAND2 expression to ventricular sidedness.

depth-cvs-emb-004.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-004.prompt: A loss-of-function mutation prevents pharyngeal endodermal SHH from activating patched receptors on secondary-heart-field cells. Which causal chain best explains the expected cardiac phenotype?
depth-cvs-emb-004.learningObjective: Trace SHH signaling from pharyngeal endoderm to outflow-tract morphogenesis.

depth-cvs-emb-005.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-005.prompt: NOTCH signaling through JAG1 is disrupted within the secondary heart field. Which downstream event is most directly reduced before conotruncal septation fails?
depth-cvs-emb-005.learningObjective: Connect NOTCH-JAG1 signaling to FGF-dependent neural crest behavior.

depth-cvs-emb-006.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-006.prompt: Cephalic folding occurs normally, but lateral body-wall folding is experimentally prevented. Which cardiac abnormality follows most directly?
depth-cvs-emb-006.learningObjective: Distinguish the cardiac effects of cephalic and lateral embryonic folding.

depth-cvs-emb-007.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-007.prompt: The middle portion of the dorsal mesocardium fails to disappear. Which normal adult pericardial feature would be absent or obstructed?
depth-cvs-emb-007.learningObjective: Explain formation of the transverse pericardial sinus from dorsal mesocardium.

depth-cvs-emb-008.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-008.prompt: A lineage tracer labels mesenchymal cells at the caudal border of the dorsal mesocardium. Which later combination should contain descendants of these labeled cells?
depth-cvs-emb-008.learningObjective: Trace proepicardial-organ descendants into the epicardium and coronary vasculature.

depth-cvs-emb-009.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-009.prompt: Myocardium forms around the endocardial tube but cannot secrete its normal hyaluronic-acid-rich extracellular matrix. Which later event is most directly compromised?
depth-cvs-emb-009.learningObjective: Relate cardiac jelly to endocardial-cushion morphogenesis.

depth-cvs-emb-010.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-010.prompt: An intervention reduces flow selectively through one embryonic aortic arch while leaving angioblast formation intact. Which principle best predicts the long-term defect?
depth-cvs-emb-010.learningObjective: Apply the role of embryonic blood flow to aortic-arch selection.

depth-cvs-emb-011.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-011.prompt: A fate map labels only right-sided secondary-heart-field cells before they enter the arterial pole. In a normally patterned embryo, where should many labeled cells appear?
depth-cvs-emb-011.learningObjective: Use secondary-heart-field fate mapping to explain outflow spiraling.

depth-cvs-emb-012.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-012.prompt: At day 24, a heart tube shows normal looping. Which paired displacement should be observed?
depth-cvs-emb-012.learningObjective: Predict normal three-dimensional movements during cardiac looping.

depth-cvs-emb-013.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-013.prompt: A focal lesion destroys the middle third of the bulbus cordis while sparing its proximal and distal thirds. Which adult regions are most directly affected?
depth-cvs-emb-013.learningObjective: Differentiate derivatives of the three bulbus-cordis segments.

depth-cvs-emb-014.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-014.prompt: After looping, trabeculation appears immediately proximal and distal to the primary interventricular foramen, while the intervening bulbar region remains smooth. Which identification is correct?
depth-cvs-emb-014.learningObjective: Identify primitive ventricular regions by their relationship to the interventricular foramen.

depth-cvs-emb-015.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-015.prompt: An embryo establishes normal organ situs, but the cardiac tube bends leftward instead of rightward during days 22-28. Which finding is most directly attributable to this later event?
depth-cvs-emb-015.learningObjective: Separate a local looping defect from earlier whole-body laterality defects.

depth-cvs-emb-016.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-016.prompt: At the middle of week 4, a catheter placed in either sinus horn would encounter inflow from the same three paired venous systems. Which set is correct?
depth-cvs-emb-016.learningObjective: Identify the original paired venous inputs to the sinus venosus.

depth-cvs-emb-017.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-017.prompt: During week 5, the right umbilical vein and left vitelline vein regress as venous return is redirected. Which combined morphologic response should follow?
depth-cvs-emb-017.learningObjective: Explain rightward sinus-venosus remodeling from left-to-right venous shunts.

depth-cvs-emb-018.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-018.prompt: A specimen at 10 weeks retains only the normal definitive remnants of the left sinus horn. Which pair should be present?
depth-cvs-emb-018.learningObjective: Identify both definitive derivatives of the left sinus horn.

depth-cvs-emb-019.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-019.prompt: The superior part of the right venous valve regresses normally, but its inferior part persists and differentiates. Which adult structures should arise from that inferior part?
depth-cvs-emb-019.learningObjective: Trace the inferior right venous valve into its two adult remnants.

depth-cvs-emb-020.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-020.prompt: An internal right-atrial ridge separates a smooth posterior region from a trabeculated appendage. Which developmental boundary does the ridge preserve?
depth-cvs-emb-020.learningObjective: Interpret the crista terminalis as an embryologic boundary.

depth-cvs-emb-021.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-021.prompt: Proliferation at the caudal end of the dorsal mesocardium is selectively blocked while septum primum still descends. Which defect most directly follows?
depth-cvs-emb-021.learningObjective: Explain how the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion positions the pulmonary vein.

depth-cvs-emb-022.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-022.prompt: Early in development, one pulmonary-vein stem opens into the left atrium and divides into four branches outside it. How do four separate atrial openings normally arise?
depth-cvs-emb-022.learningObjective: Explain how pulmonary-vein incorporation produces four left-atrial openings.

depth-cvs-emb-023.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-023.prompt: A laterality defect shifts the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion moderately to the right rather than keeping it near the midline before leftward positioning. Which drainage pattern is most directly predicted?
depth-cvs-emb-023.learningObjective: Predict TAPVR anatomy from displacement of the dorsal mesenchymal protrusion.

depth-cvs-emb-024.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-024.prompt: At autopsy, a narrow oblique cleft remains between septum primum and septum secundum, but there was no chronic interatrial shunt. Which interpretation is most accurate?
depth-cvs-emb-024.learningObjective: Distinguish probe patency from a hemodynamically significant atrial septal defect.

depth-cvs-emb-025.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-025.prompt: A lineage marker labels cells that delaminate from endocardium into extracellular matrix but does not label cardiac neural crest. In which cushion population should labeled mesenchyme predominate?
depth-cvs-emb-025.learningObjective: Compare cellular origins of atrioventricular and conotruncal cushions.

depth-cvs-emb-026.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-026.prompt: A mutation disrupts extracellular-matrix deposition and cell migration in both atrioventricular and conotruncal cushions. Which combination of structures is simultaneously at risk?
depth-cvs-emb-026.learningObjective: Integrate the multiple septal, valvar, and outflow roles of cushion tissue.

depth-cvs-emb-027.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-027.prompt: Two adjacent regions of a chamber wall expand rapidly while a narrow intervening strip grows slowly. The expanding walls approach and merge. What distinguishes the resulting septum from a cushion-built septum?
depth-cvs-emb-027.learningObjective: Compare cushion fusion with septation by differential chamber-wall growth.

depth-cvs-emb-028.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-028.prompt: A precisely timed insult acts from day 27 through day 37, when the embryo grows from about 5 mm to 16-17 mm. Which process is most broadly vulnerable during this interval?
depth-cvs-emb-028.learningObjective: Place major cardiac septation within its vulnerable developmental interval.

depth-cvs-emb-029.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-029.prompt: Programmed cell death in the upper septum primum is experimentally delayed until after the lower edge has fused completely with the endocardial cushions. Which immediate hemodynamic problem is expected?
depth-cvs-emb-029.learningObjective: Explain why ostium secundum forms before ostium primum closes.

depth-cvs-emb-030.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-030.prompt: Which arrangement creates a one-way flap route for fetal blood rather than a simple hole through a single septum?
depth-cvs-emb-030.learningObjective: Describe the two-septum architecture of the fetal foramen ovale.

depth-cvs-emb-031.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-031.prompt: At birth, placental flow stops and the lungs expand. Which pressure sequence directly closes the foramen ovale?
depth-cvs-emb-031.learningObjective: Integrate pulmonary and placental changes in functional foramen-ovale closure.

depth-cvs-emb-032.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-032.prompt: At the end of week 4, four cushions surround the AV canal. Which fusion is specifically required to produce separate right and left AV orifices by the end of week 5?
depth-cvs-emb-032.learningObjective: Identify the cushion fusion that divides the common AV canal.

depth-cvs-emb-033.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-033.prompt: At first, the common AV canal opens only into the primitive left ventricle. Which later change allows atrial blood direct access to both primitive ventricles?
depth-cvs-emb-033.learningObjective: Explain how AV-canal realignment establishes access to both ventricles.

depth-cvs-emb-034.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-034.prompt: During AV-valve formation, the bloodstream hollows the ventricular surface of cushion-derived mesenchyme. What transformation completes the supporting apparatus?
depth-cvs-emb-034.learningObjective: Trace AV-cushion mesenchyme into leaflets, chordae, and papillary attachments.

depth-cvs-emb-035.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-035.prompt: Prenatal ultrasound shows loss of the normal four-chamber cross at the AV junction. A single AV orifice has abnormal leaflets separating an atrial opening from a ventricular opening. Which developmental failure best explains all findings?
depth-cvs-emb-035.learningObjective: Infer persistent AV canal from the four-chamber cross and combined septal components.

depth-cvs-emb-036.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-036.prompt: An embryo has partial, rather than complete, fusion of the atrioventricular endocardial cushions. Which structural combination best matches that mechanism?
depth-cvs-emb-036.learningObjective: Distinguish the septal consequences of partial versus complete atrioventricular-cushion fusion failure.

depth-cvs-emb-037.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-037.prompt: Complete obliteration of the right AV orifice prevents direct right-atrium-to-right-ventricle flow. Which compensatory constellation is required or expected in the described defect?
depth-cvs-emb-037.learningObjective: Reason through the obligatory shunts and chamber changes in tricuspid atresia.

depth-cvs-emb-038.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-038.prompt: A tricuspid valve is displaced toward the right-ventricular apex. Which chamber geometry follows most directly?
depth-cvs-emb-038.learningObjective: Predict chamber remodeling from apical tricuspid-valve displacement.

depth-cvs-emb-039.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-039.prompt: During week 5, the right-superior and left-inferior truncus swellings grow distally while winding around each other. What is the functional consequence of their normal geometry?
depth-cvs-emb-039.learningObjective: Explain why conotruncal ridges spiral during outflow alignment.

depth-cvs-emb-040.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-040.prompt: After fusion, the conus septum divides the conus into an anterolateral channel and a posteromedial channel. Which mapping is correct?
depth-cvs-emb-040.learningObjective: Map conus compartments to definitive ventricular outflow tracts.

depth-cvs-emb-041.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-041.prompt: The muscular ventricular septum forms normally, but tissue from the anterior inferior AV cushion does not extend across its superior rim. Which fusion fails to complete the membranous septum?
depth-cvs-emb-041.learningObjective: Integrate AV cushion, conus, and muscular components in membranous septation.

depth-cvs-emb-042.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-042.prompt: Partitioning of the truncus is nearly complete in week 7. Two tubercles lie on the main truncus swellings, and a third appears opposite them in each channel. What next produces functional semilunar cusps?
depth-cvs-emb-042.learningObjective: Explain formation of three semilunar cusps by tubercle hollowing.

depth-cvs-emb-043.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-043.prompt: A morphologic left ventricle lies on the right and connects to the right atrium through a mitral valve, while the morphologic right ventricle lies on the left and connects to the left atrium through a tricuspid valve. Which developmental disturbance best fits?
depth-cvs-emb-043.learningObjective: Recognize ventricular inversion as a laterality and cardiac-specification defect.

depth-cvs-emb-044.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-044.prompt: Two infants have similar ostium-secundum atrial defects. In one, septum primum is excessively fenestrated; in the other, its flap is present but lacks an adequate rim to overlap. What distinguishes the second mechanism?
depth-cvs-emb-044.learningObjective: Differentiate the two major morphologic mechanisms of ostium-secundum ASD.

depth-cvs-emb-045.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-045.prompt: The foramen ovale closes before birth while pulmonary vascular resistance remains high. Which remodeling pattern most directly follows?
depth-cvs-emb-045.learningObjective: Predict chamber consequences of prenatal foramen-ovale closure.

depth-cvs-emb-046.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-046.prompt: Anterior displacement of the conotruncal septum divides the conus unequally. Which finding is a secondary hemodynamic consequence rather than a direct geometric partitioning defect?
depth-cvs-emb-046.learningObjective: Separate primary conotruncal geometry from secondary pressure remodeling in tetralogy.

depth-cvs-emb-047.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-047.prompt: Why is persistent common truncus arteriosus expected to coexist with a ventricular septal defect?
depth-cvs-emb-047.learningObjective: Link persistent truncus to obligatory failure of membranous ventricular septation.

depth-cvs-emb-048.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-048.prompt: The conotruncal septum forms but descends straight rather than spiraling. Which ventriculoarterial connections result?
depth-cvs-emb-048.learningObjective: Infer ventriculoarterial connections from loss of conotruncal spiraling.

depth-cvs-emb-049.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-049.prompt: A neonate with a 22q11 deletion has facial anomalies, thymic hypoplasia, parathyroid dysfunction, and a conotruncal defect. Which shared developmental failure best unifies the craniofacial and cardiac findings?
depth-cvs-emb-049.learningObjective: Use neural crest lineage to connect pharyngeal and conotruncal abnormalities.

depth-cvs-emb-050.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-050.prompt: A fetus has pulmonary valvular atresia with a severely narrowed pulmonary trunk. Which shunt direction becomes essential for pulmonary perfusion after birth?
depth-cvs-emb-050.learningObjective: Reason through ductal dependence in pulmonary valvular atresia.

depth-cvs-emb-051.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-051.prompt: Complete fusion of the aortic semilunar cusps causes aortic atresia and marked left-heart hypoplasia. How are the ascending aorta and coronary arteries supplied in the illustrated fetal pattern?
depth-cvs-emb-051.learningObjective: Explain retrograde coronary perfusion in fetal aortic atresia.

depth-cvs-emb-052.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-052.prompt: The heart is exposed on the surface of the chest, but intracardiac looping and septation are otherwise intact. Which developmental process most directly failed?
depth-cvs-emb-052.learningObjective: Identify the morphogenetic failure responsible for ectopia cordis.

depth-cvs-emb-053.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-053.prompt: A lineage map follows the dominant pacemaker as the heart develops. Which sequence is correct?
depth-cvs-emb-053.learningObjective: Trace relocation of pacemaker activity into the definitive sinoatrial node.

depth-cvs-emb-054.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-054.prompt: A developmental lesion destroys the specialized cardiac-myocyte population coalescing around the AV canal but spares sinus-venosus tissue. Which function is most directly lost?
depth-cvs-emb-054.learningObjective: Relate AV-node origin to its relay position in the conduction pathway.

depth-cvs-emb-055.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-055.prompt: Which lineage statement correctly distinguishes intrinsic conduction tissue from its autonomic regulation?
depth-cvs-emb-055.learningObjective: Differentiate myocardial conduction-system origin from autonomic innervation.

depth-cvs-emb-056.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-056.prompt: TBX3 cannot function in a cluster of primary cardiac myocytes that would normally become conduction tissue. Which cell-fate error is most direct?
depth-cvs-emb-056.learningObjective: Explain how TBX3 permits conduction-system differentiation.

depth-cvs-emb-057.subject: embryology
depth-cvs-emb-057.prompt: Angioblasts coalesce to form a dorsal aorta, after which smaller vessels sprout from established channels. Which classification is correct?
depth-cvs-emb-057.learningObjective: Distinguish vasculogenesis from angiogenesis using a major-vessel example.

depth-cvs-hist-071.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-071.prompt: Two medullary epithelial-reticular populations are compared. Population X forms a desmosome-linked framework throughout the medulla; population Y forms concentric keratin-rich whorls. Which pairing is correct?
depth-cvs-hist-071.learningObjective: Differentiate the two major medullary epithelial-reticular specializations.

depth-cvs-hist-072.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-072.prompt: A thymocyte can bind self MHC appropriately but reacts strongly to a self peptide. What is its expected fate as it moves through thymus?
depth-cvs-hist-072.learningObjective: Apply the sequential logic of positive and negative thymic selection.

depth-cvs-hist-073.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-073.prompt: An older adult has extensive thymic adipose replacement with only small islands of cortical and medullary lymphoid tissue. Which functional consequence best follows?
depth-cvs-hist-073.learningObjective: Relate thymic involution to T-cell output.

depth-cvs-hist-074.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-074.prompt: A palatine tonsil biopsy shows a stratified squamous lining so densely infiltrated by lymphocytes that its boundary is difficult to recognize. Why is this finding functionally appropriate?
depth-cvs-hist-074.learningObjective: Explain why tonsillar crypt epithelium is lymphocyte-rich.

depth-cvs-hist-075.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-075.prompt: A specialized epithelial cell over a Peyer patch lacks a typical brush border and has a deep basolateral pocket containing lymphocytes and dendritic cells. What is its principal role?
depth-cvs-hist-075.learningObjective: Relate M-cell morphology to mucosal antigen sampling.

depth-cvs-hist-076.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-076.prompt: A particulate antigen enters an afferent lymphatic on the convex surface of a lymph node. Which route does it follow before leaving at the hilum?
depth-cvs-hist-076.learningObjective: Trace lymph through the compartments of a lymph node.

depth-cvs-hist-077.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-077.prompt: A cortical lymphoid nodule has a pale center of large proliferating lymphoblasts surrounded by a darker ring of small naive lymphocytes. Which labels are correct?
depth-cvs-hist-077.learningObjective: Identify the zones of a secondary lymphoid follicle.

depth-cvs-hist-078.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-078.prompt: Naive lymphocytes leave blood through vessels lined by unusually cuboidal endothelial cells after L-selectin binding. In which lymph-node compartment should these vessels be sought?
depth-cvs-hist-078.learningObjective: Localize HEVs and connect their endothelial form to lymphocyte entry.

depth-cvs-hist-079.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-079.prompt: A medullary compartment contains many plasma cells with eccentric nuclei next to reticular channels carrying antibody-rich lymph. Which pairing is correct?
depth-cvs-hist-079.learningObjective: Differentiate medullary cords from medullary sinuses.

depth-cvs-hist-080.subject: histology
depth-cvs-hist-080.prompt: Blood leaves sheathed capillaries into splenic cords before reentering sinusoids through slits between stave cells. Which consequence follows most directly?
depth-cvs-hist-080.learningObjective: Explain how open splenic circulation tests erythrocyte deformability.

depth-cvs-phys-001.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-001.prompt: A drug suppresses the rapid ventricular phase-0 upstroke but does not directly inhibit L-type calcium channels. Which comparison with the sinoatrial node is most accurate?
depth-cvs-phys-001.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: Fast sodium-current block directly depresses ventricular phase 0 more than the nodal calcium-dependent upstroke.

depth-cvs-phys-002.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-002.prompt: An isolated ventricle receives a second ordinary stimulus halfway through its first contraction. Why does this fail to produce skeletal-muscle-like summation?
depth-cvs-phys-002.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: Most of the contraction coincides with an action-potential refractory period.

depth-cvs-phys-003.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-003.prompt: Immediately after an isolated rise in aortic pressure, preload and intrinsic contractility are initially unchanged. Which first-beat change is expected?
depth-cvs-phys-003.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: More blood remains at end systole and stroke volume falls.

depth-cvs-phys-004.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-004.prompt: Two beats have the same 120-mL end-diastolic volume. End-systolic volume falls from 60 to 40 mL after a positive inotropic stimulus at unchanged afterload. What happens to ejection fraction?
depth-cvs-phys-004.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: It rises from 50% to approximately 67%.

depth-cvs-phys-005.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-005.prompt: Atrial fibrillation removes coordinated atrial contraction. Which normal atrial pressure feature is directly lost, rather than simply shifted in timing?
depth-cvs-phys-005.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: The a wave.

depth-cvs-phys-006.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-006.prompt: Why can losing atrial contraction cause more symptoms in a patient with a stiff ventricle than in a healthy resting subject?
depth-cvs-phys-006.learningObjective: Apply electrical events, pump mechanics, and pressure interpretation: A stiff ventricle relies more on the late atrial contribution to filling.

depth-cvs-phys-007.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-007.prompt: A rigid vessel initially has inlet/outlet pressures of 110/10 mm Hg. Both rise by 20 mm Hg without changing resistance. What happens to flow?
depth-cvs-phys-007.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: It remains unchanged because the driving pressure difference is still 100 mm Hg.

depth-cvs-phys-008.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-008.prompt: In an ideal laminar vessel, radius doubles and viscosity also doubles; length and pressure gradient remain fixed. What is the new flow relative to baseline?
depth-cvs-phys-008.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: Eight times baseline.

depth-cvs-phys-009.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-009.prompt: Two identical vascular beds, each of resistance R, run in parallel. One becomes completely occluded, and perfusion pressure stays constant. What happens to total flow?
depth-cvs-phys-009.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: It halves because equivalent resistance rises from R/2 to R.

depth-cvs-phys-010.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-010.prompt: At fixed blood velocity, vessel diameter, and density, anemia lowers viscosity. What combined prediction follows from the ideal flow relationships?
depth-cvs-phys-010.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: Resistance falls while the tendency toward turbulence increases.

depth-cvs-phys-011.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-011.prompt: Stroke volume remains 70 mL while effective arterial compliance falls from 2 to 1 mL/mm Hg. Using the simplified SV/compliance estimate, how does pulse pressure change?
depth-cvs-phys-011.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: It increases from 35 to 70 mm Hg.

depth-cvs-phys-012.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-012.prompt: A pulse is detected rapidly at the wrist after ventricular ejection. What travels from the aorta to the wrist much faster than the average blood itself?
depth-cvs-phys-012.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: A pressure/distension wave through the arterial system.

depth-cvs-phys-013.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-013.prompt: In a stated classical Starling model, Pc = 30, Pi = −2, plasma oncotic pressure = 25, and interstitial oncotic pressure = 3 mm Hg; reflection coefficient = 1. What is the net outward driving pressure?
depth-cvs-phys-013.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: 10 mm Hg outward.

depth-cvs-phys-014.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-014.prompt: Venous drainage from a limb is obstructed while arterial inflow persists. Which immediate change most directly promotes local edema?
depth-cvs-phys-014.learningObjective: Apply hemodynamic calculations and competing vascular effects: An increase in upstream capillary hydrostatic pressure.

depth-cvs-phys-015.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-015.prompt: At steady state, oxygen consumption is 300 mL/min, arterial oxygen content 20 mL/dL, and mixed-venous content 14 mL/dL. What is cardiac output?
depth-cvs-phys-015.learningObjective: Apply cardiac output, venous return, and coronary supply–demand: 5 L/min.

depth-cvs-phys-016.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-016.prompt: Mean systemic filling pressure is 9 mm Hg and resistance to venous return is 2 mm Hg/(L/min). If right atrial pressure rises from 1 to 5 mm Hg with the other values fixed, how does venous return change?
depth-cvs-phys-016.learningObjective: Apply cardiac output, venous return, and coronary supply–demand: It falls from 4 to 2 L/min.

depth-cvs-phys-017.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-017.prompt: A patient has elevated measured right atrial pressure, reduced ventricular filling, and low output caused by pericardial compression. Which interpretation is best?
depth-cvs-phys-017.learningObjective: Apply cardiac output, venous return, and coronary supply–demand: Elevated intracavitary pressure does not ensure adequate transmural distending pressure.

depth-cvs-phys-018.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-018.prompt: Marked tachycardia worsens left-ventricular ischemia despite a higher heart rate. Which paired mechanism best explains this?
depth-cvs-phys-018.learningObjective: Apply cardiac output, venous return, and coronary supply–demand: Less diastolic coronary perfusion time together with greater myocardial oxygen demand.

depth-cvs-phys-019.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-019.prompt: During sympathetic cardiac stimulation, coronary flow rises even though some coronary vessels have constrictor alpha receptors. Why is this not a contradiction?
depth-cvs-phys-019.learningObjective: Apply cardiac output, venous return, and coronary supply–demand: Increased myocardial metabolism produces local vasodilation that can outweigh direct vasoconstriction.

depth-cvs-phys-020.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-020.prompt: A laboratory preparation converts fibrinogen to fibrin normally but cannot covalently stabilize the resulting fibrin network. Which missing activity best explains this?
depth-cvs-phys-020.learningObjective: Apply from platelet adhesion to stable clot: mechanism discrimination: Activated factor XIII.

depth-cvs-phys-021.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-021.prompt: Tissue factor exposure is intact, but functional factor X is absent. Why can the intrinsic pathway not fully rescue thrombin generation?
depth-cvs-phys-021.learningObjective: Apply from platelet adhesion to stable clot: mechanism discrimination: Both pathways require the common factor-X/prothrombinase step for efficient thrombin generation.

depth-cvs-phys-022.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-022.prompt: After prolonged obstruction of bile delivery, a patient produces inadequately gamma-carboxylated clotting factors. What link best explains the defect?
depth-cvs-phys-022.learningObjective: Apply from platelet adhesion to stable clot: mechanism discrimination: Reduced absorption of fat-soluble vitamin K impairs factor maturation.

depth-cvs-phys-023.subject: physiology
depth-cvs-phys-023.prompt: A local injury activates platelets, while adjacent healthy endothelium helps prevent uncontrolled recruitment. Which pair best represents this opposing endothelial effect?
depth-cvs-phys-023.learningObjective: Apply from platelet adhesion to stable clot: mechanism discrimination: Nitric oxide and prostacyclin.
